summary: This program is the bakery's starting point: it creates one plain cookie and one decorated cookie, then prints the description each object gives of itself.

lines.text: A separate class holds the application logic, keeping the program that uses cookies apart from the classes that define what a cookie is.
Java starts every program at main, so this is where the sample objects get built.
The new keyword builds a Cookie object in memory and passes its flavor to the constructor; the variable regular is how we reach that object later.
A DecoratedCookie is created the same way, because a subclass is used exactly like the class it extends.
Calling describe() on the object asks it to build its own description string, which is the object-oriented alternative to printing its fields from outside.
The identical call on the decorated cookie produces different output, since the subclass supplies its own version of describe().
